Right-biased and left-biased U.S. news outlets differ in their coverage of Discrimination & Toxicity AI risks in terms of the focus and language used. Right-biased outlets (36.1% of their articles) emphasize risks related to the false portrayal of historical figures, such as "the founding fathers as people of color" by AI, and express concerns about AI systems like ChatGPT producing responses that are skewed against conservatives and in favor of leftists. They also highlight issues related to bias in content moderation systems, noting that negative comments about women are more likely to be flagged as hateful compared to similar comments about men.

In contrast, left-biased outlets (24.9% of their articles) focus on the inclusion of far-right and non-reputable sources in AI training data, which they argue leads to the dissemination of hate speech through AI responses. They also report on the negative impacts of AI technologies on marginalized groups, such as financial discrimination against people of color due to biased algorithms.

The language used in right-biased outlets tends to be politicized, framing the risks in a way that aligns with their agenda on freedom of expression and concerns about a perceived culture war. Left-biased outlets, on the other hand, use language that emphasizes social justice and the harmful effects of AI on marginalized communities.
